channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
item.description: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.

item.title: [ECFR] A future with Chinese characteristics
item.description: The world is undergoing a historical and cultural rupture. Just as Hollywood and other American exports once gave the rest of the world a glimpse of modern life and the future that awaited them, China is now doing the same for African, Latin American and even American young people

item.title: [ECFR] Friends without benefits: Why the EU should offer Canada more than casual defence ties
item.description: Trump is pushing Canada—a quiet military powerhouse—away from America. The EU should seize the chance and fold it into its own defence

item.title: [Financial Times] Russian warship fires flares at Danish helicopter over Baltic Sea
item.description: Denmark says one of the flares passed the aircraft at close range, branding the action as ‘reckless’

item.title: [Financial Times] Scott Bessent’s wobbly house
item.description: Politics seems to be messing with the US Treasury secretary’s head

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs scrap ‘kill switch’ on EU carbon border levy
item.description: MEPs voted to strip the European Commission of a proposed power to temporarily exempt goods (such as fertilisers) from the EU's carbon border levy, setting up a clash with member states.

item.title: [EU Observer] The Pope, Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon just handed Brussels a mandate to rein in AI
item.description: When Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon take the stage together to call for responsible AI development, and Pope Leo XIV does so in his encyclical Magnifica Humanitas, all aligning with the direction of EU regulation, there is political space for urgent action.

item.title: [ECFR] Life of the party: Democrats and the search for a post-Trump future
item.description: The race for US midterms reveals a rapidly changing Democratic party. Europeans must understand and engage its three camps well before the party could take power

item.title: [EU Observer] State of the Union: Three shocks Ursula von der Leyen isn’t prepared for
item.description: Here are three crises Ursula von der Leyen probably won't mention on Wednesday in her State of the Union address: a US financial crash, sanctions on China, and taking on Big Tech's algorithms.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU countries to discuss AI rules as Trump calls safety warnings a ‘hoax’
item.description: Officials are set to gather in Brussels this week amid growing calls for regulation, including from key figures in the tech industry.

item.title: [EU Observer] Sweden Democrats’ ‘era of deportations’ leaves lasting mark across Europe as Stockholm forms new government
item.description: As the final ballots are counted before an official result on Wednesday, Sweden's outgoing government was one tainted with one of the strongest deportation rates and most stringent migration policies in the EU.

item.title: [EU Observer] No circular economy without good working conditions
item.description: Europe’s Circular Economy Act can reduce dependencies, strengthen industrial resilience and create skilled green jobs. But it will only succeed if workers, working conditions and social dialogue are placed at its heart.

item.title: [Politico Europe] World Trade Organization reform failure could cost 10% of global GDP, report warns
item.description: The document says that the current trading system is facing its worst disruption in 80 years.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Sabotage suspected as parts of Dutch rail network come to a standstill
item.description: A Dutch minister called the alleged sabotage "particularly worrying."

item.title: [Financial Times] Ten-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2007
item.description: Benchmark bond yield rises to 5.04% and stocks fall amid concerns over inflation and higher interest rates

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech — live updates
item.description: European Commission president sets out her vision for the future of the continent.

item.title: [DW] Netherlands: Suspected sabotage disrupts train services
item.description: A major outage has hit parts of the Dutch railway system after objects were found placed across lines, authorities say. The company responsible for rail infrastructure says it suspects deliberate wrongdoing.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Carney presses 10 EU countries to ratify Canada trade deal
item.description: The Canadian prime minister is seeking to deepen ties with Europe amid a trade war with the U.S.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Will ‘Made in Europe’ spark a new trade battle with the US?
item.description: A single EU fund for “strategic projects” has become a major standoff, putting US steel tariffs, supply chains, and transatlantic relations at risk.

item.title: [DW] Europe launches two climate observation satellites
item.description: The European Space Agency has put two satellites into orbit to take a closer look at the impact of climate change. One of them will focus particularly on plant life.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Rayner v Streeting, round two
item.description: As the TUC Congress continues in Brighton, some of Labour’s big beasts have been baring their teeth – with Angela Rayner using an after-dinner speech to land some blows on Defence Secretary Wes Streeting. Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy reveal what was said and whether it was all taken in good fun. Meanwhile, the economic […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Alarm in Denmark after Russian ship fires at military helicopter
item.description: "It is part of the pattern we see throughout Europe," Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen warned on Tuesday morning.

item.title: [EU Observer] What competitiveness experts expect from von der Leyen’s State of the Union
item.description: For our new report, Economic Competitiveness and European Citizens, we asked 11 experts from across Brussels and beyond 12 questions about Europe’s competitiveness debate. Download it for free here.

item.title: [Financial Times] China’s economy shows signs of weakness as investment slumps
item.description: Deteriorating domestic indicators add pressure on policymakers to increase stimulus spending

item.title: [Politico Europe] Can less paperwork get EU workers moving?
item.description: Why is it easier for a jar of peanut butter to cross EU borders than it is for a European worker? According to the Commission, varying social security systems and professional qualifications make it hard for Europeans to work outside their home country in the bloc. The EU executive’s Fair Labour Mobility Package — unveiled […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Houthi advances leave Trump with only bad choices
item.description: Washington appears loath to step into another front as new oil disruptions send prices soaring.

item.title: [Financial Times] War ‘on all fronts’ tests Saudi Arabia’s crown prince
item.description: Two-pronged assault by Houthi rebels and Iraqi militants has spawned what may be biggest test for Prince Mohammed since backlash against Jamal Khashoggi’s murder

item.title: [Financial Times] Putin moves flagship summit over drone threat
item.description: Russian president has avoided Black Sea coast for nearly a year amid Ukrainian attacks

item.title: [Financial Times] How Poland lost $230mn trying to buy Venezuelan oil with crypto
item.description: An attempt to use digital currencies for a bold oil trade became one of Poland’s biggest scandals

item.title: [Financial Times] US equities eclipse Treasuries in rare foreign capital shift
item.description: International flows into American equities exceed government debt for first time this century outside pandemic and aftermath of global financial crisis

item.title: [Politico Europe] Deutschlands Weg aus dem Bildungsdesaster
item.description: Deutschlands Bildungssystem befindet sich im freien Fall. Nach dem jüngsten PISA-Schock belegt nun auch der neue Bildungsmonitor eine Abwärtsspirale, die jeden Bildungspolitiker und die Regierung alarmieren müssen. Maximilian Stascheit analysiert die Lage und präsentiert fünf konkrete Thesen, wie durch einen Fokus auf Basiskompetenzen und ungeschönte Daten die Trendwende gelingen kann. Im 200-Sekunden-Interview erklärt Bildungsministerin Karin […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Supreme Court rejects Trump’s mail-in ballot restrictions for midterms
item.description: Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented in an unsigned decision that comes weeks before congressional elections

item.title: [Financial Times] Russian businessman bankrolls Donald Trump Jr’s Bahamas wedding after-party
item.description: President’s son and his wife confirm Umar Kremlev, who is reportedly close to Vladimir Putin, paid for part of celebration

item.title: [Financial Times] China tightens control of overseas travel in sweeping new law
item.description: President Xi Jinping steps up efforts to secure state secrets, advanced technology and highly skilled workers

item.title: [ECFR] Future nostalgia: Europe’s unfinished song
item.description: ECFR’s new research reveals Europeans are suffering from an imagination gap. Many people want to see Europe strong and flourishing—but fewer can picture a credible route from today’s disruptions to that destination

item.title: [ECFR] Beyond Saxony-Anhalt: What Merz’s crisis means for Europe
item.description: The far-right AfD’s win in a small German state calls for dynamism in Berlin and hedging in Brussels

item.title: [ECFR] Emergency Room: The AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Jana Puglierin, senior policy fellow and head of ECFR’s Berlin office, to discuss the Alternative for Germany (AfD)’s election win in Saxony-Anhalt—and what it means for Germany and Europe

item.title: [ECFR] Britons back ban on trade with Israeli settlements by more than two to one
item.description: New polling published by ECFR shows that Britons across the political divide favour banning trade with illegal Israeli settlements

item.title: [DW] Are electric cars really bad for the environment?
item.description: Some German politicians are calling for a delay to the EU plan to phase out gas-powered vehicles, saying cars must be judged on the entire carbon footprint. But the full picture still says EVs are more climate friendly.

item.title: [ECFR] Booted, then suited: Veterans and the making of Putin’s new proto-elite
item.description: The Kremlin is promoting Ukraine war veterans--cultivating a proto-elite who could reinforce Russia’s militarised course.

item.title: [DW] Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
item.description: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

item.title: [DW] Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
item.description: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia has affected their lives.

item.title: [DW] A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
item.description: Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he avoided making his ethnic background a theme of his art for fear of being pigeonholed. Then it became his focus.

item.title: [DW] Russia's drone war comes to Moldova and Romania
item.description: Incursions by Russian drones into Moldovan and Romanian airspace are increasingly common. This week the Ukrainian president's plane was stopped from taking off from Chisinau. Observers suspect the attacks are deliberate.

item.title: [DW] DW exclusive: Zelenskyy offers to meet Putin at G20 in Miami
item.description: In an interview with DW, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was in a strong position to negotiate and offered to meet Vladimir Putin in Miami.

item.title: [Financial Times] US military reveals it has weapons in space
item.description: Security experts warn announcement could result in the proliferation of weapons by other governments

item.title: [EU Observer] Fighting fossil-fuel inflation with ECB rate hikes punishes renewables, research finds
item.description: Every 10-percent rise in oil and gas prices increases overall inflation by 0.35 percentage points. The European Central Bank's rate hikes risk making it worse by making renewable investments more expensive, finds the London-based research institute New Economics Foundation.

item.title: [DW] EU seeks Arctic strategy amid growing power rivalry
item.description: Russia's aggression, Trump's threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe's agenda.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks
item.description: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get through the winter.

item.title: [EU Observer] Canada’s Carney’s ‘unique alliance’ with the EU? It’s already being built
item.description: A pro-EU technocrat, Mark Carney is the sort of politician Brussels loves to do business with.

item.title: [DW] Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
item.description: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing; Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners" on any such move.

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech risks making border pushbacks ‘normal’ EU migration policy
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen is expected to announce new migrant-busting proposals on Wednesday during her State of the Union speech in Strasbourg. Speculation is rising on what they could be, given the bloc has spent 10 years debating asylum reforms which only kicked into force three months ago.

item.title: [EU Observer] Was it coincidence Russia attacked the railway used by Johnson and the former CIA chief? Three takeaways from the strike near Nato’s border
item.description: A strike just six kilometres from Poland’s border has jolted Warsaw and Kyiv into openly debating whether Nato should start flexing its own muscles along the frontier to force Vladimir Putin to pull troops away from Ukraine.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU extends Russia sanctions for one week only, after France insists on delisting Usmanov
item.description: Paris could be bartering with Baku to free a French businessman jailed for spying, in return for dropping EU sanctions against a Russian oligarch with friends in high places.

item.title: [EU Observer] Croatia’s toxic waste dump scandal shows the cost of Europe’s ‘forever chemicals’
item.description: Some 45,000 tonnes of hazardous plastic and medical waste lies uncollected and polluting groundwater in Croatia more than a year after it was discovered — prompting street protests in Zagreb, whilst chemical industry lobbyists in Brussels push for more exemptions for 'forever chemicals'

item.title: [EU Observer] Putin sends a 14th century saint’s hand to Ukraine front to boost morale (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,663)
item.description: Putin has paraded a medieval saint’s severed hand before frontline troops, as Russian forces grind forward around Orikhiv and drones openly hunt Kherson civilians.

item.title: [DW] EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
item.description: Russia's drone attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border has triggered EU calls to up support for Kyiv. Allies of Ukraine should show they "are not scared," said the bloc's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.

item.title: [EU Observer] Leipzig was a warning shot. Here’s what real deterrence against Kremlin terror would look like
item.description: The wave of Russian state terrorism now breaking over Europe is quite different from the leftwing Baader-Meinhof group of the 1970s. It is part of a big plan to break Nato, yet Germany (and Spain, France, and Belgium) is not taking this seriously. This sends a clear message to the Kremlin: keep attacking us, writes Edward

item.title: [ECFR] Against war, drought and hunger: A global coalition to prevent a food crisis
item.description: Three features of today’s unordered world are converging to create a devastating food crisis. Russia’s war in Ukraine is disrupting agricultural exports from both countries. The enduring blockage of the Strait of Hormuz is restricting fertiliser shipments. And this year’s El Niño (a sporadic warming of the Pacific Ocean generating widespread knock-on effects elsewhere) could […]

item.title: [ECFR] Remembering Emma Bonino
item.description: ECFR founding member and co-chair emerita Emma Bonino has died at the age of 78. A towering figure in European foreign policy, she was an inspiration to millions across the continent. She left a deep mark on European and Italian politics, and on ECFR

item.title: [ECFR] The EU’s unfinished business in the Western Balkans
item.description: Montenegro and Albania are moving closer to EU membership. But Brussels should not forget its responsibility towards the Western Balkans as a whole

item.title: [DW] Turks in Germany anxious after AfD wins in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: The Alternative for Germany party's win in Saxony-Anhalt has alarmed people of Turkish origin in eastern states. Will workers and business owners abandon the increasingly AfD-friendly region for the more welcoming west?

item.title: [DW] Magyar vs. Moscow: Hungary toughens stance toward Russia
item.description: Prime Minister Peter Magyar has abruptly ended the era of his predecessor's warm relations with Russia: Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats. The Kremlin is considering halting gas supplies in response.

item.title: [ECFR] The geopolitics of global hunger
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Cary Fowler and Jim O’Brien to discuss the factors behind the escalating risk of a major food crisis—and Europe’s role in preventing catastrophe

item.title: [ECFR] Ukraine: The battle beyond war
item.description: Jessica Hendrick welcomes Roman Petrov and Svitlana Zalishchuk to discuss Ukraine’s simultaneous fight for survival on the frontlines and battle for democracy at home

item.title: [ECFR] Orchestrators, not customers: A new role for European governments in defence
item.description: Weapons that took decades to develop can now be countered within months. European governments need to stop buying finished platforms and start running an innovation cycle, in which soldiers learn from one system and build these lessons into the next

item.title: [ECFR] Bonus episode: The EU enlargement game
item.description: In a special episode recorded live from Lisbon, Jessica Hendrick puts six EU candidate countries through an enlargement simulation to find out what happens when crisis, cash, disinformation and political pressure collide with the race to join the EU
